result:
No trace-logger code in this repo, so I'll go on what you've described.

The dedup logic has a real gap for your stated use case: it keeps only the **first entry's response**, but for a flaky API being retried 40-50 times, the responses are almost certainly *not* identical across calls — that's usually why the caller is retrying (errors, timeouts, partial results, rate-limit responses, etc.). By collapsing on request-args equality alone, you're storing "called N times" but silently discarding what actually happened on calls 2 through N — which is precisely the signal you'd need to explain why a run cost more or produced a different outcome.

Concretely:
- If call #14 returned a 500 and #15 returned valid data (and the agent used that data), your trace now just shows "called 40x, see first response" — no way to tell which call succeeded, how many failed, or what the failures looked like.
- Per-call latency/timestamps are also collapsed into one, so you lose the ability to see if the run was slow because of retry backoff.
- "Ran it against last week's incident traces and the counts line up" only validates that you preserved *count*, not that you preserved the *content* needed for incident analysis — it's not actually testing the thing you rely on traces for.
- This week's traces are already in the new format, so for any collapsed run, the discarded per-call responses aren't recoverable unless you have raw logs elsewhere.

I'd suggest tightening the dedup condition (or the retained data) before this becomes the only record you have of a real incident:
- Only collapse when the **response** also matches the first call, not just the request args — genuinely-identical repeated calls (e.g., redundant reads) are safe to fold, but retries-after-failure are not.
- If you still want to collapse retries for size, keep a lightweight per-occurrence record (status/error code, latency, response hash or size) instead of dropping them entirely — that's a small fraction of the payload size but preserves the diagnostic signal.
- Worth checking whether the original per-call raw traces are archived anywhere (even short-retention) so this week's incident data isn't permanently reduced to counts.

I'd flag this to your teammate/reviewer before it becomes the default for future weeks, since as-is it looks like it optimizes away exactly the data you said you rely on it for.
